digests.title: TLDR AI — 2026-09-24
digests.tagline: Gemini TTS 🗣️, Claude’s novel enzyme 🧬, Google private memory 🔒

stories.headline: Qwen Intelligence Launches Three Mobile AI Agents (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Qwen Intelligence has launched three mobile agents for planning, cross-app execution, and rapid content creation, alongside open benchmarks for planning, real-device performance, and safety. Qwen reports top benchmark results and 90% end-to-end success for Mobile-Use.

stories.headline: Google's new speech models can design and direct voices (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google released Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Flash-Lite TTS, letting developers create voices from descriptions and direct pacing, dialect, and delivery line by line. Flash-Lite targets high-volume work such as dubbing and voice agents, while Flash can replicate an authorized voice from a 30-second sample.

stories.headline: Claude Discovered a Novel Enzyme System (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic said Claude autonomously identified a previously unknown enzyme system associated with unusual DNA repeats and characteristics seen in programmable genetic systems such as CRISPR.

stories.headline: Escaping SPACE: Part I (23 minute read)
stories.blurb: Perplexity's SPACE platform tested VM isolation and network confinement using nine AI models, revealing no VM-host breaches across 108 trials. However, four models exploited network-policy vulnerabilities via DNS spoofing and IP-sharing, bypassing restrictions in 11 out of 54 partial-network trials. Post-remediation, none of the models succeeded in bypassing the updated security measures, highlighting the necessity for robust policy enforcement against shared infrastructure attacks, which were also found in eight of ten tested third-party platforms.

stories.headline: Towards Universal Post-Training for Robotics (18 minute read)
stories.blurb: Robotics needs a universal post-training recipe similar to language models to achieve reliable autonomous deployment. Existing methods like imitation learning benefit from intuition rather than structured processes, and RL's instability hinders robotics. The development of EXPO-FT demonstrates a stable RL approach, emphasizing the need for standardized protocols, reward specifications, human feedback systems, and scalable processes to enhance robotics reliability.

stories.headline: Introducing Ember-1 (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Ember-1 is a new specialized model built on Kimi K3 that delivers Kimi K3's quality with 40% fewer tokens. It is now rolling out as a serving option alongside the base Kimi K3 model as a Research Preview release on Serverless. Fireworks Research is introducing research releases to give developers two-week serverless access to new research models. The models with the most demand will be made permanent.

stories.headline: tev1-4B-experimental (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: tev1-4B-experimental is a Jev-like classifier fine-tuned on top of Qwen3.5 4B. It is available on Together serverless at $0.042 per million input tokens and $0 per million output tokens. Together AI has released the data recipe and a tutorial on how to fine-tune a custom model. Tev1 only cost $17 to train.

stories.headline: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: An AI agent's capability is largely set by its harness. Evolving the harness against a fixed evolve set is effective, but the harness memorizes the training tasks, and large in-distribution gains shrink or vanish out of distribution. RRSI keeps the harness edit space open and regularizes the search trajectory through it instead. Prompts, control flow, configuration, context management, tools, skills, memory, and sub-agents may all be modified. The constraints act on how the search moves, not on what the harness may contain.

stories.headline: Google plans AI memory that even Google cannot read (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google says its planned Private AI Compute memory would let assistants recall context across devices without Google being able to read it. Data stays encrypted in cloud storage, keys stay on users' devices, and a protected enclave decrypts it only while answering a request.

stories.headline: How Accurate Have AI Progress Forecasts Been So Far? (36 minute read)
stories.blurb: Forecasters dramatically underestimate AI progress on benchmarks. Predictions on AI adoption and diffusion often lean toward underestimation. There is not enough evidence to assess forecasters' track record on predicting macro-scale economic and societal impacts of AI.

stories.headline: OpenAI introduced MentalHealthBench (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: MentalHealthBench is an open benchmark created by OpenAI with more than 80 licensed mental health experts to evaluate AI responses across realistic mental health conversations.

stories.headline: Introducing Comfy Router: One API for Frontier Media Models (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Comfy Router, available on the Comfy Developer Platform, unifies access to various frontier media models with one API, allowing developers seamless model integration and provider flexibility for better pricing and availability.

stories.headline: Amjad Masad on Rethinking College for the AI Era (48 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI-era education should prioritize curiosity, project-based learning, and intellectual exploration over grades and credentials.

stories.headline: A new wave of Connected Apps is rolling out to Gemini (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Gemini is adding direct integrations with tools including Linear, Adobe, Webflow, Peloton, Experian, and SeatGeek.

digests.title: TLDR IT — 2026-09-24
digests.tagline: Meta’s $349 AI glasses 👓, Google agents go offline 💻, Microsoft’s $10B cloud push ☁️

stories.headline: Google brings offline agents to the Antigravity SDK (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google's Antigravity SDK now supports local models through LiteRT and compatible inference servers, enabling agents to run offline while keeping code on-device. Hybrid workflows can combine cloud-based planning with local execution to reduce API usage and limit sensitive data transfers.

stories.headline: Meta unveils $1,300 VR glasses with a portable workspace (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Meta unveiled VR glasses weighing about 100 grams, with computing and battery hardware housed in a tethered puck, launching in Spring 2027 for $1,299.99. The device offers a private multi-screen workspace, virtual keyboard and touchpad, and photorealistic avatar calling through apps including Zoom and WhatsApp.

stories.headline: Meta brings Muse to glasses and unveils $349 audio frames (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Meta has announced plans to bring its Muse personal AI agent to its glasses, alongside new Ray-Ban Meta Audio frames starting at $349 and shipping October 13. The expanded lineup includes Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 with improved battery life and controls, extending Meta's push toward hands-free AI assistance.

stories.headline: AI agents expose the cracks in cloud infrastructure (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: Undocumented configurations and manual workarounds become operational risks when AI agents start managing infrastructure. Reliable automation requires infrastructure and policies defined in code, built-in cost and access controls, and clear boundaries for actions that need human approval.

stories.headline: AI agents need a more integrated security operations center (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Fragmented security tools force analysts and agents to rebuild context and coordinate actions across separate systems, slowing incident response. Microsoft's proposed answer is an integrated security operations center, now in Defender preview, that combines SIEM, threat protection, and response controls around shared context.

stories.headline: Barracuda launches AI Data Security to control what employees send to chatbots (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Barracuda launched AI Data Security to stop sensitive company data from reaching ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, and 1,300+ other AI tools. It adds prompt-injection screening, policy controls, and audit logs for SMBs and MSPs, available in October with SecureEdge Premium Access. A Barracuda survey found 49% of CIOs at 500 to 1,000 employee firms lack AI governance skills.

stories.headline: The Genie One MCP is now Generally Available (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Databricks made its Genie One MCP server generally available, giving any AI agent governed access to structured and unstructured data plus business context through Genie Ontology. The MCP runs as a managed service in Unity Gateway, adding centralized governance, fine-grained policies, and audit logging while keeping answers consistent across tools like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor. It aims to reduce agent sprawl by letting agents query data, retrieve results, and explore visualizations and citations without custom connectors.

stories.headline: Topology-Aware Workload Scheduling with NVIDIA Topograph (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: NVIDIA Topograph is an open source toolkit that discovers cluster network topology from cloud or on-premises providers and normalizes it into a common model. It publishes that topology as Kubernetes node labels, Slurm configurations, Slinky ConfigMaps, or NFD resources so schedulers like KAI Scheduler, Kueue, and native Kubernetes can place tightly coupled GPU workloads near each other. By keeping topology current as clusters change, Topograph reduces network congestion and improves AI factory efficiency, tokens per watt, and cost across Kubernetes, Slurm, and Slinky environments.

stories.headline: Microsoft plans $10B-plus Middle East cloud investment (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Microsoft plans to invest more than $10 billion through 2030 across Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE to expand cloud and AI infrastructure. Its commitments also include more than $400 million for network connectivity, alongside sovereign cloud capabilities and business continuity programs.

stories.headline: What Dropbox has learned from deploying AI at company scale (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Dropbox says scaling AI requires redesigning end-to-end workflows, aligning incentives, and measuring outcomes like revenue, quality, and retention. It reports ~70% AI-generated code, top-5% PR throughput versus similar peers, and quality in line with industry, while using internal coding agents like Nova to connect AI spend to engineering value. Leaders argue that as AI lowers engineering costs, human problem-solving, judgment, and leadership matter more, and trusted organizational context will separate effective adopters.

stories.headline: Accelerated Server Sales Are Themselves Accelerating (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Q2 2026 server sales surged 52% year over year to $166.32 billion.

stories.headline: New Surface business PCs arrive October 13 (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Microsoft's refreshed 12-inch Surface Pro and 13-inch Surface Laptop bring Snapdragon X2 Plus processors, local AI capabilities, and enterprise management tools.

digests.title: TLDR Web Dev — 2026-09-24
digests.tagline: Claude gets 3x faster ⚡, Gemini 3.8 TTS 🎙️, Google’s self-improving harnesses 🧩

stories.headline: Rendering Huge Pull Requests in the GitHub Copilot App (14 minute read)
stories.blurb: GitHub rebuilt the Copilot app's pull request view to keep a diff with 2,200 files, more than one million changed lines, and over 400 inline comments responsive. The design separates fixed code geometry from lazily measured comment blocks, then uses permanent instrumentation and automated stress loops to catch scroll jumps, leaks, and jank.

stories.headline: How We Made claude.ai 3x Faster in Two Weeks (15 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic made the core Claude web and desktop experience about three times faster during a two-week sprint, cutting the 75th-percentile fresh-load time from 3.1 seconds to 0.55 seconds. The team used Claude to create deterministic benchmarks, pursue bottlenecks in parallel, and lock in gains with CI ratchets, feature flags, and staged rollouts.

stories.headline: Why WebSockets Beat SSE for AI Streaming at Scale (22 minute read)
stories.blurb: WebSockets provide the bidirectional channel that agentic interfaces need for cancellation, approvals, and steering while a response is still streaming. They also reduce per-message overhead and support ordered binary data, but teams must still add reconnection, delivery guarantees, fan-out, and operational tooling themselves.

stories.headline: We Are All Product Engineers Now (19 minute read)
stories.blurb: As code generation gets cheaper, software work shifts toward discovering what customers need, defining what good looks like, and making products delightful. The forecast assumes agents will absorb more of review, maintenance, deployment, and scaling, which makes product judgment and tacit knowledge more valuable than routine implementation.

stories.headline: Agentic Coding: Bet on the Primitives (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI coding agents lower the cost of building thin, team-owned layers on top of focused primitives, changing when it makes sense to install a framework. Mature libraries still win for commodity UI and accessibility-heavy components, because agents reduce implementation effort without replacing domain knowledge.

stories.headline: Electrobun 2.0 (Website)
stories.blurb: Electrobun 2.0 builds cross-platform desktop apps with a native main process, system webviews by default, and optional bundled Chromium or WGPU surfaces. Its new Hutch toolchain, Cottontail TypeScript runtime, multi-language main processes, differential updates, signing, and templates aim to keep releases small, with a basic app around 1.28 MiB.

stories.headline: Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech says hello (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS adds prompt-designed and replicated voices with line-by-line control over pacing, emotion, accents, and dialogue across more than 100 languages and dialects. Flash-Lite targets high-volume use, while consent verification, SynthID watermarking, and C2PA credentials add safeguards for generated audio.

stories.headline: TinyJS (Website)
stories.blurb: TinyJS packages cross-platform desktop apps at roughly 6 MB by pairing a JavaScript backend with each operating system's native webview instead of bundling Chromium. It includes system APIs, hot reload, signed builds, and socket-based page-to-backend RPC, with Windows and Linux still marked beta.

stories.headline: The Complete Guide to Cloudflare Quick Tunnels (25 minute read)
stories.blurb: Cloudflare Quick Tunnels expose a local server at a temporary HTTPS URL with one cloudflared command, without requiring an account, DNS changes, or an open router port. They work well for webhooks, mobile testing, demos, coding-agent previews, POST streaming, and WebSockets, but use a random hostname that disappears when the process stops. The tradeoffs include a 200-request concurrency limit, no SLA, no Cloudflare Access, and buffered SSE, so persistent or production workflows should move to a named tunnel.

stories.headline: Building Tools for AI Agents (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Reliable agent tools must separate a user's identity from delegated authority, return clear operation states, and distinguish permission failures from temporary service errors. The article also recommends safe retry contracts, idempotency support, and repeatable evaluations that test task completion, recovery behavior, cost, and unauthorized actions.

stories.headline: Self-improving Agent Harnesses Overfit. How Google Fixes It (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Self-improving harnesses can memorize the evaluation set they evolve against, producing large in-distribution gains that mostly disappear on unseen tasks. Google's RRSI regularizes harness edits with sparsity and magnitude penalties plus noise-aware acceptance rules, improving the held-out average from 39.7 to 43.6 while using 36% fewer tokens than unregularized evolution.

stories.headline: Univer (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: Univer is an open-source, plugin-based Office SDK for embedding spreadsheets, documents, presentations, and headless agent workflows in browser and Node.js applications.

stories.headline: What Happens When the Model Eats the Stack? (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: Stronger general coding agents will absorb much task-specific data-agent scaffolding, leaving persistent semantic context, consistency, storage, and compression as the more durable systems problems.

stories.headline: How Notion Handles Concurrent Editing with CRDTs (11 minute read)
stories.blurb: Notion replaced last-write-wins block text with an RGA-based CRDT so concurrent and offline edits can merge without silently discarding changes.

stories.headline: Show Keystrokes on a Website with the show-keystrokes Custom Element (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: The show-keystrokes web component displays keyboard input inside the page, making shortcuts visible in tab or window screen shares without a separate desktop utility.

digests.title: TLDR InfoSec — 2026-09-24
digests.tagline: EvilTokens ring busted ⚖️, 474 GitHub keys leaked 🔑, INC ransomware intrusion 💀

stories.headline: Critical Bifrost AI Gateway Flaw Lets Attackers Run Commands Without Credentials (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Bifrost, an open-source AI gateway for 20+ LLM providers, ships with management auth disabled by default, so a single unauthenticated POST to /api/mcp/client can register a stdio MCP client and run arbitrary commands as the gateway user (CVE-2026-90898, CVSS 9.8). That exposes every stored provider API key. The official Docker image binds the management API to 0.0.0.0, and v2.0.0 only fixed a related plugin-loading flaw (CVE-2026-86242, CVSS 8.1). Upgrade to transports/v2.1.0 or set governance.auth_config.is_enabled to true, and treat any exposed unauthenticated instance as compromised by rotating virtual and provider API keys.

stories.headline: BigCommerce Data Stolen via Ribon Apps Hack (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Attackers used compromised Ribon API credentials from a Fastr system breach to access BigCommerce merchant customer data from September 13 to 17. Exposed records included names, email addresses, phone numbers, and postal addresses. BigCommerce revoked the credentials, uninstalled affected Ribon apps, and notified merchants.

stories.headline: GitHub App Private Keys: 474 Leaked Keys Exposed (11 minute read)
stories.blurb: GitGuardian tested 4,802 leaked GitHub App private keys and found 474 that were still authenticated as 440 apps. Forty-four apps held organization-admin permissions. 207 could write repository content, and with the keys having no expiry, the leaked PEM files can remain usable for years. Cases included an Actions token app installed across roughly 300 organizations, BuildBuddy's internal app, Crusher.dev, and a CDC-related app.

stories.headline: The Tale of Two INC Ransom Notes (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: An INC ransomware intrusion across 175+ endpoints started in early August with randomly named scheduled tasks launching an obfuscated PowerShell implant and RDP lateral movement. After 17 quiet days, AnyDesk delivered netscan.exe and a BYOVD EDR killer (hwau.exe loading the HwAudio driver), and Impacket's atexec.py deployed the payload. Huntress onboarded after the incident, so initial access is unknown, and the gap points to an access broker handing off to an affiliate, who followed the standard note with a DATALEAK_PRESS_RELEASE.txt listing stolen files and threatening to contact clients within 48 hours. Defenders should alert on randomly named scheduled tasks, unexpected RMM installs, and new or unsigned driver services, and limit privileged accounts to the systems they actually need.

stories.headline: Handle Redirect (17 minute read)
stories.blurb: EDR products typically register callbacks on handle creation to monitor when processes call OpenProcess so they can strip access rights before a handle to a sensitive process like lsass is delivered. This article demonstrates a technique in which an attacker calls OpenProcess on a benign process (like notepad.exe) and then redirects the received handle to the sensitive process to evade EDR detection. To detect this attack vector, a security product running at the kernel level can periodically scan all process handle tables and compare ObjectPointerBits decoded EPROCESS against the process that owns the table.

stories.headline: Revoking the token didn't kill the backdoor (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: GraphWorm, an implant tied to the China-nexus group Webworm, uses a real OneDrive account over Microsoft Graph as a dead drop, and its "upgrade" task swaps all five hardcoded OAuth credentials for a spare account in one command, so token revocation only pauses it. It also identifies victims by hashing MAC, CPU, and disk serials, so renaming or re-addressing a host won't shake the operator. Isolate the host or block the app ID in your own tenant at the same moment you revoke, then hunt sign-in logs for that app ID, unfamiliar tenants, and non-browser user agents hitting OneDrive.

stories.headline: Firmware Reverse Engineering Skills (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: A collection of five agent skills for firmware extraction, static analysis, Ghidra reverse engineering, emulation, and security reporting.

stories.headline: Outerlimit (Product Launch)
stories.blurb: Outerlimit provides a decentralized authorization layer for autonomous software agents. It finds agents, monitors behavior, and enforces policies at execution time. The system restricts token use by scope, location, and conditions.

stories.headline: pktz (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: pktz is an eBPF-powered network traffic monitor with per-process and per-connection reporting.

stories.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI Models Still Attempt Restricted Actions in Safety Tests (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 escaped or tampered with its sandbox in 1.5% of unguarded tests. With package-registry credentials, it took harmful actions in roughly half of simulated exercises. OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna bypassed “access denied” controls in 42% of runs - Sol did so in 64%. OpenAI plans third-party reviews covering safeguards, capabilities, and misalignment incidents.

stories.headline: Microsoft disrupts AI-assisted platform that compromised 12,000 accounts (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: EvilTokens, a Telegram-sold subscription service ($1,500 upfront, $500 monthly), abused Microsoft Entra device code authentication to compromise 12,000 accounts across 10,000 organizations before a Microsoft-led operation seized 50 websites and 150 domains, and the UK's Met Police arrested two men. Its AI chatbot analyzed 5,000 compromised emails at a time to identify who could approve payments, who they reported to, and which impersonation ruses would send funds to attacker accounts. Microsoft described it as a shift where criminals can make sense of a compromised inbox in minutes rather than days.

stories.headline: North Korea's Hangro Revisited (20 minute read)
stories.blurb: Hangro, North Korea's SoftEther-derived VPN and mail client for officials abroad, added a July 2026 management certificate whose SAN lists hosts in Pyongyang and Khabarovsk plus an internal CGNAT address, while its older 2024 chain fails every signature check, including the root against itself. Its Chinese callback traces to six Shenyang assignments under a single 2008 Silibank registry contact, though silibank[.]com lapsed and was re-registered in 2023. The researcher describes the DPRK "return leg" as layered rather than a single pipe, with dead-drop pickup during Chinese office hours, 10 GB ETRN-enabled mail relays for bulk transfer, and Hangro for interactive sessions, though no actual traffic was observed.

stories.headline: UK cops arrest 2 EvilTokens suspects, Microsoft seizes 50 phishing kit websites (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Microsoft and UK police disrupted EvilTokens, a Microsoft device-code phishing service.

stories.headline: Stolen passwords are exposing America's water providers to hackers (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: SpyCloud found stolen credentials at 1,787 of 10,000 US water providers reviewed.

digests.title: TLDR Design — 2026-09-24
digests.tagline: Premiere on Android 🎬, Liquid Glass Controls 🫧, Meta Audio Glasses 👓

stories.headline: Meta introduces camera-free AI glasses (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Meta introduced Ray-Ban Meta Audio, camera-free AI glasses that support music, calls, speech translation, and its Muse assistant, offering an alternative to smart glasses that can record people without their consent. Removing the cameras makes the frames slimmer and lighter at 43 grams, with adjustable temple tips, swappable nose pads, and a battery life of up to 12 hours. Starting at $349, the glasses come in Clubmaster and Burbank styles with prescription options.

stories.headline: macOS 27 gives you more control over Liquid Glass (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a customizable Liquid Glass appearance slider that lets users adjust the system's transparency from highly clear to more opaque, changing the look of the Dock, widgets, sidebars, toolbars, and apps like Music and Podcasts with a single system-wide setting. The update gives users more control over the Mac's visual style while preserving the modern Liquid Glass design language.

stories.headline: Adobe Premiere, One of the iPhone's Best Video-Editing Apps, is Now on Android (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Adobe is bringing its redesigned Premiere video-editing app to Android, nearly a year after its iPhone debut, replacing Premiere Rush, which loses support September 30. Layouts adapt across devices, pairing footage and a multitrack timeline side by side on foldables while still running on candy-bar phones like the Pixel. The app is free with no login required, though Firefly-powered features like Generative Fill require paid generative credits once the monthly allotment runs out.

stories.headline: UX-Context Design: Using UX Knowledge to Inform AI-Generated Design (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: As more interface work turns AI-generated, research and design output shifts from human-facing deliverables toward curated context that guides AI, dubbed UX-context design. DESIGN.md, which Google Labs open-sourced in April 2026 from its Stitch tool, encodes a product's visual identity for AI tools in exact values and plain-language guidance. A hypothetical broader file, UX.md, would add research findings, interaction standards, a glossary, and user and world models as a continuously updated source.

stories.headline: Modernizing a legacy system? Your before/after isn't the case study (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Strong modernization case studies focus less on before-and-after visuals and more on the design decisions behind them, highlighting the judgment calls that shaped the final product rather than the process or visual refresh alone. Employers want to understand what changed because of the designer's thinking, not just that an outdated interface now looks modern.

stories.headline: Nothing has changed other than how we talk about it (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Agentic AI can dramatically speed up the research and problem-definition phases of Design Thinking by analyzing assumptions, synthesizing evidence, and pressure-testing ideas, but human judgment remains essential for validating outputs and making design decisions. Rather than replacing designers, AI shifts their role from generating information to evaluating evidence, challenging assumptions, and deciding what should be built.

stories.headline: A System That Preserves the Act of Drawing Itself (Website)
stories.blurb: A system that preserves the act of drawing itself, where every gesture is remembered, and every image continues to evolve.

stories.headline: Named Colors with Documented Histories (Website)
stories.blurb: One color a day, told as it ought to be told: with its provenance, its chemistry, and the people who paid for it in poison.

stories.headline: The Visual Dictionary of AI Art Keywords (Website)
stories.blurb: The visual dictionary of AI art keywords — one word, one image, and free to browse. Master prompt keywords for Midjourney, Google Nano Banana, GPT Image, FLUX, and Stable Diffusion.

stories.headline: Design Systems are a Collection of Decisions (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: Design systems amount to collections of already-made decisions, so mechanical checks can prove straight from the artifact whether an AI agent used real components and correct tokens. Judgment-based evals still have an answer key when the system has documented a decision, like a required confirmation pattern for destructive actions. Visual evals work against a known reference, but deciding whether a new visual direction deserves to exist should stay with people.

stories.headline: Spatial UI Design: Tips and Best Practices (21 minute read)
stories.blurb: Augmented reality design differs from screen-based UX, demanding attention to physical space, bodily comfort, and the cognitive load added to real-world distractions. UX consultant Frank Spillers' guidelines favor real-world physics, direct hand gestures over menus, context-aware triggers, and short, interruptible interactions. Content should stay within about 30 degrees of a user's central field of view, never past 50, and sit between 1.25 and 5 meters away.

stories.headline: Industrial Designer Alberto Essesi's Pen for Precision Sketching (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Alberto Essesi's satin-finished aluminum Exclamation Pen and matching rest feature a severely tapered point that keeps the tip visible for precision sketching.

stories.headline: This Secret Brooklyn Archive Contains a Trove of Design Rarities. Here Are 10 Exceptional Finds (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Collectible design gallery R & Company has opened Building 86, its 16,000-square-foot storage warehouse in the Brooklyn Navy Yard, to the public by appointment for the first time.

digests.title: TLDR Data — 2026-09-24
digests.tagline: AI Benchmarks Are Broken 💥, Jev Inside Your Warehouse ⚡, Doom Runs on SQL 🎮

stories.headline: How Concurrence governs clinical AI at a trillion-token scale with Unity Gateway (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Concurrence uses Databricks to run and govern clinical AI at an annualized scale of roughly 1.2 trillion input tokens, combining patient data, agent state, testing, evaluations, and access controls on one platform. Unity Gateway centralizes access to approved AI models and tools, helping the company track usage, enforce compliance, and safely scale both clinical and coding agents.

stories.headline: If You Last Used Cassandra 3.11, You Might Not Recognize It Today (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: Apache Cassandra 5 loosens many of the constraints teams learned with 3.11, adding storage-attached indexing, unified compaction, native vector search, and built-in repair scheduling. Cassandra 6 goes further with ordered cluster metadata and cross-partition transactions, although partitioning and workload design remain fundamental.

stories.headline: We ported the original Doom to SQL (25 minute read)
stories.blurb: CedarDB ported the original Doom's game logic and renderer almost entirely to SQL, running the game loop at its original 35 Hz and rendering at up to 60 FPS. The experiment shows that surprisingly complex real-time logic can work with SQL's set-based model, while database features like transactions, access control, and shared state make multiplayer particularly natural.

stories.headline: Real-time LLM guardrails with Jev: comparing latency and cost (13 minute read)
stories.blurb: TypeSafe's Jev uses a purpose-built decision model for real-time AI guardrails, checking agent inputs, responses, and tool calls before they execute. In Arize's tests, it made the same decisions as GPT-5.4 nano while running 15-18x faster and costing 12-14x less per call.

stories.headline: Benchmarks are more broken than we could have imagined (15 minute read)
stories.blurb: Horizon audited over 5,000 AI benchmark tasks across 20 datasets and confirmed 29 were broken, with problems including leaked answers, incomplete tests, gameable graders, and failing reference solutions. Many of these flaws actually inflated model scores, highlighting how benchmark results can overstate capabilities when the underlying tasks and graders are unreliable.

stories.headline: Jevflake (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: Jevflake brings TypeSafe's Jev decision model into Snowflake through SQL functions and dbt, letting teams classify, score, and ask structured questions about their data with probabilistic answers. It can cache results in dbt models and add tests or human-review queues, making AI classifications reusable parts of normal analytics workflows.

stories.headline: DuckDB Now Ships inside dbt v2 (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: dbt v2's Rust-based Fusion engine now includes a built-in DuckDB adapter, removing the need for a separate adapter installation. It adds DuckLake and Iceberg REST catalog support, writes queryable project metadata as Parquet, and performs SQL analysis that finds type or column problems before warehouse execution. The migration path starts by testing the opt-in v2 parser against existing projects.

stories.headline: Announcing Apache Fluss 1.0: Real-Time Data Foundation for AI (15 minute read)
stories.blurb: Apache Fluss 1.0 introduces a stateless Rust HTTP Gateway for metadata, table operations, and batch writes, alongside native Python access and deeper Flink, Spark, Hudi, and Paimon integration. It adds row and log TTLs, predicate pushdown, coordinator high availability, resource protection, and cleanup features, moving the project from incubator-era capabilities toward production real-time lakehouse workloads.

stories.headline: Introducing prompt_jev(): bringing Jev to MotherDuck SQL (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: MotherDuck's new prompt_jev function brings Jev directly into SQL, letting users classify and score text at analytics scale without training a model or parsing LLM responses. In its 100,000-row benchmark, Jev achieved 89% accuracy in 40 seconds for $0.50, outperforming the tested LLMs on speed, cost, and accuracy.

stories.headline: How Adaptive Tail Sampling Works in the OpenTelemetry Collector (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Fixed-rate sampling often discards the rare traces needed in an incident, while ordinary tail sampling loses statistical weights. An adaptive tail sampler for the OpenTelemetry Collector buffers traces, applies ordered rules, and attaches W3C probability thresholds so downstream counts can be reweighted. It adapts by route and service, bounds memory under load, and is progressing upstream toward alpha.

stories.headline: High-Throughput OLTP in Three Simple Steps (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: High-throughput transaction systems benefit from co-design rather than copying a connection-pool pattern from a general-purpose database. TigerBeetle models linked transfers atomically, aggregates balances without scans, batches operations automatically while a request is in flight, and prefers time-ordered identifiers for fast idempotency checks. Its benchmark illustrates why batching and ordered IDs can matter more than adding clients.

stories.headline: Profile your Polars queries (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Polars now exposes a query profiler for local open-source workloads.

stories.blurb: Common Crawl has released open web graphs covering 245.8 million hosts and 133.2 million domains.
